Seminar Title:

Fabrication and Properties of Graphene-Fortified MgO-C Refractories

Seminar Type:

Department:

Ceramic Engineering

Speaker Name:

Goutam Ghosh ( Rollno : 920cr5001)

Seminar Hall, Dept. of Ceramic Engineering.

10 Jul 2026 10.00 AM.

Contact:

Debasish Sarkar

Abstract:

The increasing demand for sustainable steelmaking has driven the development of low-carbon refractory materials without compromising the in-service performance. The conventional MgO-C refractories used in steel ladle slag zone requires higher graphite content to maintain the excellent corrosion resistance and thermal shock resistance properties at application temperature. However, more graphite addition (&gt10 wt.%) in refractory causes significant CO₂ emissions and leading to oxidation-related refractory degradation. This makes the refractory porous and deteriorates the refractory properties to poor corrosion resistance, lower thermal shock performance, and limited hot strength. Hence, this research focuses on developing low-carbon MgO-C refractories with improved thermo-mechanical and corrosion-resistant properties by partially replacing the graphite with graphene.

Indigenous graphene was synthesized via a seedlac-based process, yielding few-layer graphene (&le15 layers) with a specific surface area of ~50 m&sup2/g. The graphene consists of cyclic carbon structures with functional groups that promote its reactivity throughout the refractory matrix. To ensure uniform dispersion, a co-grinding technique with MgO fines and a modified dual-route mixing approach (powder and resin incorporation) were developed. Microstructural analysis revealed the formation of in-situ nano-bonding phases, including SiC nanotubes, whiskers, and carbide networks, attributed to reactions between graphene and silicon additives. These phases significantly improved hot strength, oxidation resistance, and slag corrosion resistance. An optimum graphene addition of 0.30 wt% (0.15 wt% via resin and 0.15 wt% as powder) resulted in enhanced cold crushing strength and reduced corrosion index from 5.5% to 3.6%. The optimized composition also exhibited reduced pore size (~0.46 &mum) and lower weight loss (~10%), indicating superior densification and oxidation resistance as compared to that of the conventional systems (~14% weight loss). Further improvements were observed with low-sulfur and S&ndashSi co-doped graphene, which enhanced dispersion and promoted carbide formation. The co-doped system exhibited ~60% higher cold crushing strength, ~70% improvement in hot strength, ~65% better oxidation resistance, and considerable reduction in corrosion area from 11.75% to 4.12%. Overall, the refractory performance has been improved by approximately 20&ndash25% in plant trials. Further, this study demonstrates that graphene, particularly S&ndashSi co-doped variants, enables the design of high-performance, low-carbon MgO-C refractories that can offer a sustainable solution for advanced steelmaking applications.
